scenes.visual: Title card 'Where the Balance Sits' fades in over a pale desert scene at morning: a flat rock, low sun, a small burrow, 16:9. COLOUR MAP, the same in every scene and in the second film: heat made by metabolism, M = ORANGE tap and arrows; heat gained from sun or rock, G = YELLOW tap and arrows; the dry leak to the air = a BLUE outlet whose WIDTH is conductance, C; evaporation, E = PALE CYAN wisps; body temperature, Tb = the fill level of a tank with a RED thermometer beside it; air temperature, Ta = a GREY dashed line; the gap Tb minus Ta = a GREY double-headed bar between the two. Cartoon schematics only, no molecular structures. Any bar or flow not computed is labelled 'schematic'. Numbers appear only as on-screen text.

scenes.tts: On a desert morning, a basking iguana is warmer than the air. So is a mouse nearby. Yet the iguana makes far less heat of its own than the mouse. How can both be warmer than the air?
scenes.visual: A cartoon desert iguana lies on the rock in sun; a cartoon mouse sits in the shade nearby. Three thermometers pop up as on-screen text: 'air 30 °C', 'iguana 40 °C', 'mouse 37 °C', with a small tag 'illustrative numbers'. A small ORANGE flame icon over the iguana burns low; over the mouse it glows bright. A question mark grows over both. Question card: 'Warmer than the air: how?'
scenes.narration: On a desert morning, a basking iguana is warmer than the air. So is a mouse nearby. Yet the iguana makes far less heat of its own than the mouse. How can both be warmer than the air?

scenes.tts: Picture each body as a tank of warmth. The level in the tank is body temperature. Heat flows in, heat leaks out, and the level settles where the two match.
scenes.visual: The mouse morphs into a simple rounded tank with a RED thermometer on its side. Liquid flows in at the top and drains out at the bottom; the level rises, wobbles, then settles and holds. A GREY dashed line for air temperature sits lower on the tank wall; a GREY bar between the level and the dashed line is labelled 'gap'. Label: 'steady: in = out (schematic)'.
scenes.narration: Picture each body as a tank of warmth. The level in the tank is body temperature. Heat flows in, heat leaks out, and the level settles where the two match.

scenes.tts: Two taps fill the tank. The orange tap is heat made by the body's own metabolism. The yellow tap is heat gained from outside, from sunlight or a warm rock.
scenes.visual: An ORANGE tap inside the tank switches on, labelled 'M, heat made (metabolism)'. A YELLOW tap above the tank switches on, with a cartoon sun and rock beside it, labelled 'G, heat gained (sun, rock)'. Both streams pour into the tank and the level rises a little.
scenes.narration: Two taps fill the tank. The orange tap is heat made by the body's own metabolism. The yellow tap is heat gained from outside, from sunlight or a warm rock.

scenes.tts: The blue outlet is the dry leak. Its width is conductance, how readily heat escapes for each degree of difference. The flow also grows with the gap between body and air.
scenes.visual: A BLUE outlet near the base, labelled 'C, conductance = width of the dry leak'. The outlet widens and the BLUE outflow thickens; it narrows and the flow thins. Then the GREY dashed air line drops; the GREY 'gap' bar lengthens and the BLUE flow speeds up. On-screen: 'dry leak = C × (Tb − Ta)'; small note: 'Ta = effective dry surroundings; each heat load counted once (simple model)'.
scenes.narration: The blue outlet is the dry leak. Its width is conductance, how readily heat escapes for each degree of difference. The flow also grows with the gap between body and air.

scenes.tts: Three routes make up that leak. Radiation, conduction, and convection by moving air or water. Each can run in or out, so the leak is their net. Sunlight and a warm rock count once, in the yellow tap, not the leak.
scenes.visual: Beside the tank, the mouse sits in shade on cool ground. Three labelled arrows draw on in turn: 'radiation' between its back and a cool sky, 'conduction' from its belly into the cool ground, 'convection' as wavy wind lines pass over its skin. Each arrow flips direction once, in then out, to show it can run either way. All three merge into the tank's BLUE outlet, labelled 'net dry exchange'. Then a cartoon sun and warm rock appear and their arrows route only to the YELLOW tap, labelled 'counted once, in G'.
scenes.narration: Three routes make up that leak. Radiation, conduction, and convection by moving air or water. Each can run in or out, so the leak is their net. Sunlight and a warm rock count once, in the yellow tap, not the leak.

scenes.tts: A fourth outlet is evaporation. Water turning to vapour carries heat away, as in sweating or panting. In practice it only removes heat, and it costs water.
scenes.visual: A PALE CYAN outlet opens at the top of the tank, labelled 'E, evaporation'. Cartoon inset: a panting dog with PALE CYAN wisps leaving its mouth; a droplet on skin turning to vapour. A small water-drop counter labelled 'water spent' ticks down. The PALE CYAN arrow only ever points outward.
scenes.narration: A fourth outlet is evaporation. Water turning to vapour carries heat away, as in sweating or panting. In practice it only removes heat, and it costs water.

scenes.tts: So the level sits where heat in equals heat out. Body temperature rises above the air by the heat coming in, minus evaporation, divided by conductance.
scenes.visual: Arrows animate into a balance beam: ORANGE M and YELLOW G on the left pan; BLUE 'C × (Tb − Ta)' and PALE CYAN E on the right; the beam levels. On-screen text builds: 'M + G = C × (Tb − Ta) + E', then rearranges to 'Tb − Ta = (M + G − E) ÷ C'. The GREY gap bar on the tank is highlighted as the left side of the second line.
scenes.narration: So the level sits where heat in equals heat out. Body temperature rises above the air by the heat coming in, minus evaporation, divided by conductance.

scenes.tts: The iguana's orange tap runs small. Its yellow tap pours, from the sun above and the rock below. That inflow alone lifts it well above the air.
scenes.visual: Split screen. Left: the iguana's tank. A thin ORANGE stream; a thick YELLOW stream from a cartoon sun and rock. The level climbs well above the GREY dashed air line; the RED thermometer reads '40 °C (illustrative)'. Right half waits, dimmed.
scenes.narration: The iguana's orange tap runs small. Its yellow tap pours, from the sun above and the rock below. That inflow alone lifts it well above the air.

scenes.tts: The mouse has almost no yellow tap. Its orange tap runs strong, and fur keeps its blue outlet narrow. Its own metabolism holds it above the air.
scenes.visual: Right half lights up: the mouse's tank. The YELLOW tap is nearly closed; a thick ORANGE stream; a cartoon fur layer wraps the tank and pinches the BLUE outlet narrow. The level holds above the air line; the RED thermometer reads '37 °C (illustrative)'.
scenes.narration: The mouse has almost no yellow tap. Its orange tap runs strong, and fur keeps its blue outlet narrow. Its own metabolism holds it above the air.

scenes.tts: That is the real difference between an ectotherm and an endotherm. The words name where the heat comes from, not how warm the animal is.
scenes.visual: Labels drop onto each half: under the iguana 'ectotherm: mostly G (outside heat)'; under the mouse 'endotherm: mostly M (own metabolism)'. A crossed-out tag 'cold-blooded = cold?' fades away beside the iguana's 40 °C thermometer.
scenes.narration: That is the real difference between an ectotherm and an endotherm. The words name where the heat comes from, not how warm the animal is.

scenes.tts: Now move the mouse into colder air, with the same fur. The gap widens, and heat leaks faster. Name two ways it can hold its level.
scenes.visual: The mouse's tank alone. The GREY dashed air line slides down; the GREY gap bar stretches; the BLUE outflow speeds up and the level starts to sag. Two empty dial slots appear beside the tank, each with a question mark. Question card: 'Two ways to hold the level?'
scenes.narration: Now move the mouse into colder air, with the same fur. The gap widens, and heat leaks faster. Name two ways it can hold its level.

scenes.visual: Question card holds; the level hangs mid-sag; a small timer ring fills.

scenes.tts: Make more heat, by opening the orange tap. Or narrow the leak, by closing skin blood vessels and fluffing the fur. Every dial an animal has changes one of these terms.
scenes.visual: First dial fills: 'make more heat' and the ORANGE tap opens wider. Second dial fills: 'narrow the leak' as cartoon skin vessels pinch and fur fluffs up, and the BLUE outlet narrows. The level rises back and holds. Small labels flash on each tap and outlet: 'shivering, brown fat → M', 'basking → G', 'fur, skin blood flow → C', 'sweating, panting → E'.
scenes.narration: Make more heat, by opening the orange tap. Or narrow the leak, by closing skin blood vessels and fluffing the fur. Every dial an animal has changes one of these terms.

scenes.tts: Who turns the taps? Sensors in the skin and deep in the body report to a controller in the brain. In mammals it sits in the pre-optic area of the hypothalamus. It chooses the target temperature.
scenes.caption: Who turns the taps? Sensors in the skin and deep in the body report to a controller in the brain. In mammals it sits in the preoptic area of the hypothalamus. It chooses the target temperature.
scenes.visual: Zoom out to a cartoon mouse outline with the tank inside. Small dots on the skin and in the core send thin lines to a labelled block in the brain, 'preoptic area (hypothalamus): controller'. A dial on the block, labelled 'target temperature', clicks to a mark; thin control lines run from the block to the ORANGE tap and the BLUE outlet.
scenes.narration: Who turns the taps? Sensors in the skin and deep in the body report to a controller in the brain. In mammals it sits in the preoptic area of the hypothalamus. It chooses the target temperature.

scenes.tts: Skin sensors give early warning. Cold air on the skin can start heat-saving responses before the core has cooled at all.
scenes.visual: A gust of cold GREY air touches the skin dots; they light up and signal the controller. The BLUE outlet narrows at once, while the core's RED thermometer has not yet moved. Label: 'skin warns first (feed-forward)'.
scenes.narration: Skin sensors give early warning. Cold air on the skin can start heat-saving responses before the core has cooled at all.

scenes.visual: Hex end card. Line: 'Body temperature sits where heat in equals heat out.'
